Need final only.|Internal engineering memo: recommendation is not to buy local AI hardware as the default replacement for hosted models. Hosted models should remain the primary path for most product work because they deliver current frontier capability, fast iteration, managed scaling, and predictable access to model updates without committing engineering time to GPUs, drivers, inference servers, monitoring, and failover. Buying hardware makes sense only where requirements are specific: strict data residency, regulated workloads, sustained high-volume inference where unit economics clearly favor owned capacity, or latency-sensitive on-prem operation that cannot tolerate external calls. Absent those constraints, local purchase concentrates risk in our own operations and delays shipping.

The main cost is not the sticker price of servers but the full lifecycle: procurement, racks, power, cooling, networking, spare parts, security patching, model packaging, observability
